title: Doctors saved his life with beer
label: SAVED BY *BEER.*

lines.text: Doctors saved his life by pouring in beer.
Vietnam, twenty eighteen. At a party, he drinks homemade rice wine, laced with methanol.
In hospital, his liver turns the methanol into formic acid, which can blind you, then kill you.
But livers prefer normal alcohol. Keep the liver busy with that, and the methanol just waits.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.text: Get me beer. Lots of it.
Down a tube, one can every hour. Fifteen cans.
Meanwhile, dialysis washes the methanol out. He walks out of hospital, fully recovered.
Comment what you want to know next.

experiment.hypothesis: A true medical rescue told straight with a short plain hook (george's rule from 27 Nov) over the most striking image: a doctor feeding a can of beer down a tube into a hospital patient. First Short with a character speaking in his own voice with a moving mouth (george, 27 Nov). Tests af_bella at 1.28 against the suspense score.
experiment.fish: #280 (doctors in Vietnam saved a man's life by pumping 15 cans of beer into his body)

facts.claim: In December 2018 Nguyen Van Nhat, 48, of Quang Tri province, Vietnam, was poisoned by homemade rice wine with methanol far above legal limits after a party; he was treated at Quang Tri General Hospital.
Doctors gave him beer through a tube, about one can an hour, fifteen cans in all, alongside dialysis; he recovered and was discharged.

The liver's alcohol dehydrogenase turns methanol into formaldehyde and then formic acid, which damages the optic nerve and causes acidosis; ethanol competes for the same enzyme, so the methanol is left unconverted until dialysis removes it (fomepizole is the preferred antidote where available).
